note: Seed 303 died at every lag, and seed 202 died at lag 60, in fast chains of close obstacles at 0.69–0.73 px/ms: small cactus, small cactus, low bird in one; small, small, large cactus group in the other. v10 jumped each obstacle in the middle of its clear window, so it landed 100–180 ms later than it had to. It then jumped the next obstacle late and came down too late for the third, which was often not on screen when the first jump was decided. The previous attempt's fast drop failed the v4 hold-while-rising test because it pressed DOWN while the dino was still going up. Changes: (1) above 0.55 px/ms, jumpTiming aims about 56 ms after the earliest safe start; below that speed it stays centred as in v10, so the low-speed v4 tests still hold. (2) rising is now judged at the moment the decision takes effect, and DUCK (fast drop) is chosen only after that point, only when it is safe and clearly faster than a normal fall, and never right before a bird to duck under. (3) JUMP is pressed while still falling when the dino will surely be on the ground before the press lands (landsBeforeInput), which saves up to one decision of reaction time.
instructions:
Apply these rules in order and pick the first that matches.
1. If over is true: choose JUMP (restarts the game).
2. If player.air is true (the dino is off the ground):
  a. If threat is null: choose NOOP.
  b. If player.rising is true: choose JUMP, unless threat.duckable is true (then NOOP). Keep the key held while the dino rises so the jump reaches full height. Releasing it early cuts the jump to about 60px and the dino lands on the cactus.
  c. If threat.duckable is true: choose NOOP.
  d. If player.landsBeforeInput is true: choose JUMP if threat.jumpTiming is "ok" or "late", otherwise NOOP. The dino is back on the ground before this decision reaches the game, so the press is a fresh jump from the ground.
  e. If player.dropSafe is true: choose DUCK. DOWN in the air is a fast drop: the dino falls much faster and is back on the ground sooner for the next obstacle. Keep choosing DUCK while dropSafe stays true.
  f. Otherwise choose NOOP. The key must be released while falling so the next jump is a fresh press.
3. If threat is null: choose NOOP.
4. If threat.duckable is true: choose DUCK if threat.contact is "near" or "overlapping", otherwise choose NOOP. Keep choosing DUCK until the bird has passed.
5. If threat.jumpTiming is "ok" or "late": choose JUMP.
6. Otherwise (threat.jumpTiming is "early"): choose NOOP and wait.
Notes:
- threat is the nearest obstacle that can still hit the dino once a decision made now takes effect. Birds high enough to run under, stars and the moon are already excluded. On the frame right after a key press, the game draws only the dino. The state then carries the obstacles forward from the last full frame.
- duckable means a bird at head height that a ducking dino passes under. contact is "far" when the obstacle reaches the dino only after the next decision could act, "near" when it arrives before then, and "overlapping" when it is already in the dino's space.
- jumpTiming comes from simulating the game's jump at the measured speed, starting when a decision made now takes effect. "early" means a jump now would come down on the obstacle or meet a high bird passing overhead, or a later decision is closer to the target moment. "ok" means now is the moment. At low speed the target is the middle of the safe window. At high speed, where an obstacle not yet in view can follow closely, the target is shortly after the earliest safe jump, so the dino lands as soon as possible. The target is earlier when a following obstacle in view needs it, or when one jump can clear both close obstacles. "late" means the target has passed, so jump immediately.
- player.rising is true while the dino will still be going up when a decision made now takes effect. Until then, releasing the key would cut the jump.
- player.landsBeforeInput is true while falling when the dino will be on the ground at least one frame before a decision made now takes effect.
- player.dropSafe can be true only after the top of the jump. It means a fast drop started now (or one already under way) hits nothing and gives up no obstacle this jump still clears. A new drop must also land clearly sooner than a normal fall, and the first obstacle met after landing must not be a bird to duck under.
- player.ducking is true while the dino is ducking on the ground.

actions.description: Keep running; release all keys (stands up from a duck, lets go of the jump key)
Jump (only from the ground with a fresh press; holding it while rising gives the full-height jump), or restart the game
On the ground: duck under birds at head height (hold while the bird passes). In the air: fast drop back to the ground (hold until it lands)

tests.why: Night-mode stars (9x9 sprites high in the sky) must never show up as obstacles.
A sky decoration must never become the threat that triggers a jump.
The star that caused the mistimed jump before the small cactus must be filtered out.
With only a star and an overhead bird ahead, the dino must stay on the ground instead of jumping into the bird.
When the dino lands before the large cactus, the threat must be the cactus rather than a star, so the jump is timed to the cactus.

tests.expect: !(state.player && state.player.air === true && state.player.rising === true && state.threat !== null && state.threat.duckable !== true) || choice === 'JUMP'
tests.why: Releasing ArrowUp right after takeoff cut the jump to about 61px and the dino landed on the double small cactus. The key must stay held while the dino rises over a cactus.
At the real early-game speed (~0.37 px/ms, not the 0.7 a fixed 30ms tick gave), a large cactus 160px or more ahead is too far: a jump now comes down on it (v4 jumped at dx 171 and died).
At the measured speed, including the input delay, a small cactus 150px or more ahead must wait (v4 jumped at dx 139-145 and landed on it).

The frame after the jump press shows only the dino, because the game redraws it alone on a key press. v9 saw no obstacles there, so threat went null. The large cactus must stay the threat through that frame.
v9 released ArrowUp on the dino-only frame right after takeoff. The jump peaked at about 60px and the dino landed on the large cactus. The key must stay held while the dino rises.
Both jumps over the last large cacti were followed by a dino-only frame with no obstacles. The cactus being jumped must still be reported as the threat there.
The fatal jump was cut short because ArrowUp was released one decision after takeoff. JUMP must stay chosen while the dino rises over the cactus.
After the DUCK press, the game drew only the ducking dino, so the head-height bird vanished from the state. The bird must stay the threat until it has passed.
v9 released the duck for one decision when the bird disappeared on the dino-only frame, and the bird hit the standing dino. DUCK must stay held while the bird passes.

tests.expect: state.player === null || state.player.air === true || (state.player.dropSafe === false && state.player.landsBeforeInput === false && state.player.rising === false)
tests.why: rising, landsBeforeInput and dropSafe describe a jump in progress. On the ground they must all be false, or a model trained on the state could learn to drop or press early from the ground.

While the dino will still be rising when the decision lands, ArrowUp must stay held (v4 died from a cut jump). A fast drop or an early press must never be offered then; the previous attempt failed by pressing DOWN while rising.

tests.expect: !(state.over !== true && state.player && state.player.air === true && state.player.rising !== true && state.player.dropSafe === true && state.threat && state.threat.duckable !== true) || choice === 'DUCK'
tests.why: v10 jumped a small cactus late, fell at normal speed, and was hit in the air by the low bird that followed. Once past the top of the jump, with a fast drop safe and clearly faster, DOWN must be pressed so the dino lands sooner.

tests.expect: !(state.over !== true && state.player && state.player.air === true && state.player.landsBeforeInput === true && state.threat && state.threat.duckable !== true && (state.threat.jumpTiming === 'ok' || state.threat.jumpTiming === 'late')) || choice === 'JUMP'
tests.why: At lag 60, v10 waited for a frame showing the dino on the ground before pressing JUMP. That cost up to a whole decision, and the dino came down in front of the large cactus group with no time left. When the dino will have landed before the press reaches the game and the timing is ok or late, JUMP must be pressed now.
